top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Possible Ouster Amid Scandal
points: Nvidia's board is deliberating whether to remove CEO Jensen Huang following reports of an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, creating a conflict-of-interest concern.
This compounds earlier allegations that Huang had a separate affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising national security concerns given Nvidia's role in US-China chip policy.
Nvidia shares fell sharply in premarket/after-hours trading (reported variously down 7% to roughly $160, and down about 25-30% over the past month, erasing around $1.5 trillion in market value).
No clear successor has been named; analysts speculate chief engineer Ian Buck or CFO Colette Kress could step in, while the board reportedly works with outside firms on a search.
Elon Musk said it would be 'an honor' to hire Huang if he departs; betting markets are pricing in his exit.
Rival chipmakers AMD and Broadcom (and Alphabet, per one report) are rallying on speculation they could gain market share if Nvidia's leadership is disrupted.
Morgan Stanley removed Nvidia from its top picks list and Baird downgraded the stock to Neutral, comparing Huang to the Icarus myth despite praising Nvidia's technical lead.
Analysts warn an 'espionage-tainted reputation' could linger for years regardless of legal outcomes, with potential FBI and Congressional inquiries looming.

The scandal arrives as a US-China trade truce is set to expire in January, complicating matters since Huang had served as an informal diplomat on chip trade policy (including lobbying for and against China export restrictions on H20/H200 chips).

unique_angles.point: Yorkville Ives estimates Nvidia's fair value would fall 25% to $225/share without Huang versus $300/share if he stays; 59% of Seeking Alpha subscribers had expected him to stay.
Huang allegedly donated $25 million to the Trump administration's ballroom project, raising crony capitalism concerns given his access on China policy.

Despite the crisis, Nvidia shares actually rose 2.9% to $173.73 ahead of its November 17 earnings report, diverging from the broader AI sector recovery; the company represents about 8% of the S&P 500.

Nvidia's 10-member board includes members with backgrounds ranging from Taco Bell international operations to academic research, and must decide whether to remove the only CEO the company has ever had, who oversaw a 700,000% share price increase.
The New York Times broke the affair story while the Wall Street Journal reported on the board's ouster deliberations; Nvidia stock is down roughly 25% since early October.
Reports indicate Nvidia is actively searching for CEO replacement candidates, suggesting a formal succession process is already underway.

top_stories.title: CoreWeave Earnings Beat Sparks AI Infrastructure Sector Rally
points: CoreWeave (an AI cloud computing infrastructure company) reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% year-over-year and ahead of analyst estimates.

Stock surged about 24-25% in a single day, its largest gain since June 2025, despite having fallen roughly 40% in the prior month on default insurance cost spikes; shares remain about 56% below their May peak of $137.98.

Company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0-$13.3 billion and pledged to avoid unsecured debt markets through 2027, plus announced a shift toward borrowing tied to actual customer orders rather than costlier unsecured debt.
The earnings beat reignited confidence across AI infrastructure names, lifting AMD (up 36.7%), Nebius (up 28.5%), Broadcom, Intel, TSMC, ASML, Micron, and SK Hynix.
The market's fear gauge VIX (a measure of expected S&P 500 volatility) dropped to 17.49 from 28.18 in one week, and the S&P 500 recaptured all of November's losses, gaining 1.3% on the day.

top_stories.title: Wall Street Reassesses Fed Rate Path as Hikes Return to the Table
points: Bank of America and JPMorgan both called the Fed's October pause (decision to hold rates steady) a 'policy mistake,' arguing policymakers are falling behind persistent inflation.
Wall Street banks now forecast additional rate increases in January and March 2025, with Goldman Sachs specifically expecting a third hike in March.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller has proposed a 50 basis point (0.5 percentage point) 'jumbo' hike for December based on October inflation data showing elevated prices across food, rent, medical care, and electronics.

unique_angles.point: Three consecutive months of hot inflation data have shifted consensus toward at least a 25 basis point December hike.

items.title: Microsoft's Cash Flow Advantage Over AI Rivals

items.title: US Credit Card Debt Hits Record as Consumers Lean on Borrowing
points: US credit card balances rose $22 billion in Q3 to a record $1.28 trillion, with interest rates near 20%, the highest since December 2024.
Credit card delinquencies rose 0.3 percentage points to 6.87% of accounts overdue, signaling growing household financial strain.
Holiday spending is expected to exceed $1 trillion this season per the National Retail Federation, likely pushing credit card debt even higher.

items.title: Brazil's Pesticide Problem Extends Beyond Borders
points: Brazil uses more pesticides than any other country, and banned toxic chemicals continue entering the supply chain via illicit imports and trade diversions despite government prohibitions.
Water tests and trade data traced the pathway of banned pesticides, revealing a gap between policy and enforcement.
Farmworkers, including on tobacco farms, spray pesticides without protective equipment, exposing them to health risks from supposedly prohibited chemicals.

items.title: Young Chinese Consumers Shift From Luxury to Value Brands
points: Young Chinese shoppers are abandoning premium luxury labels for better-value alternatives like Coach and Ralph Lauren, boosting these brands' China sales by over 30%.
The shift reflects younger demographics prioritizing value and quality over brand prestige, bucking a broader retail slump in China.

items.title: Ukraine Ceasefire Push and Alaska Senate Race Outstanding

Alaska remains the only outstanding US Senate race, with control of the chamber potentially hinging on the result.

points: Stock futures are declining ahead of Thursday's market open, signaling a broadly negative trading session.
Treasury yields (the annual return on U.S. government bonds) have risen, indicating investors are adjusting portfolios amid market uncertainty.

sections.title: Jensen Huang's Leadership Crisis at Nvidia
points: Reports reveal alleged romantic relationship between Huang and Kimberly Powell, senior Nvidia executive running healthcare business, creating direct conflict of interest as she reported directly to him.

Second scandal compounds earlier disclosure of extramarital affair involving alleged Chinese spy with geopolitical/national security implications; workplace misconduct now seen as more damaging to his employment prospects.

points: Nvidia's $1.5 trillion market value loss in one month threatens broader AI market stability, as company serves as backbone of AI revolution and carries heavy weighting in major stock indexes.

Board working with outside firms to identify CEO candidates, indicating formal succession process underway despite Huang's historical tight grip on company strategy and operations.

sections.title: Geopolitical Context: China Trade and National Security
points: In April 2025, U.S. banned H20 chip exports to China, but Huang lobbied against restrictions; ban was lifted months later and Trump administration allowed Nvidia to ship advanced H200 products to China with 25% payment to Washington.
Debate centers on whether U.S. sales to China preserve American AI leadership and dependence, or risk accelerating Beijing's development of AI systems for intelligence and military purposes.
Huang allegedly donated $25 million to Trump administration's ballroom project, raising crony capitalism concerns amid broader questions about his access to administration officials on China policy.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: Wall Street thinks the Fed made a mistake

headlines: Wall Street now expects the Fed to raise rates in December and possibly again in January, after three consecutive months of stubborn inflation data; analysts say the October pause was a policy mistake.
CoreWeave surged 24% on improved earnings and a shift to borrowing tied to customer orders, reigniting the entire AI infrastructure sector including Nvidia, AMD, and semiconductor suppliers.
Nvidia plunged in after-hours trading after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with another Nvidia executive; the board may be preparing to oust him amid ongoing scandal.
US credit card balances hit a record $1.28 trillion in Q3 as Americans rely on borrowing to maintain spending amid inflation; credit card interest rates near 20%, the highest since December 2024.

sections.title: Fed Rate Hikes Likely to Resume After Hot Inflation Data
points: Three straight months of elevated inflation across food, rent, medical care, and electronics has shifted Wall Street consensus toward at least a 25 basis point (0.25%) rate hike in December.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller has already proposed a 50 basis point (0.5%) 'jumbo' hike for December based on October inflation data, with some analysts now forecasting additional hikes in January and March 2025.

Bank of America and JPMorgan both characterized the Fed's October hold (decision not to raise rates) as a policy mistake, arguing central bankers are falling behind inflation rather than staying ahead of it.
Goldman Sachs forecasts a third rate increase will occur in March 2025, signaling Wall Street expects a more aggressive tightening cycle than previously expected.

sections.title: CoreWeave Earnings Stabilize AI Infrastructure Rally
points: CoreWeave reported better-than-expected quarterly results with higher revenue and lower losses, and announced it will shift to debt tied to actual customer orders instead of more expensive unsecured borrowing.

The 24% surge in CoreWeave (despite still being down significantly for the month) provided the catalyst that reignited confidence in AI infrastructure companies, lifting AMD, Broadcom, Intel, TSMC, ASML, Micron, and SK Hynix.

The S&P 500 recaptured all losses from November as the AI infrastructure trade rebounded, with the index gaining 1.3% on the day; however, CoreWeave still carries substantial expensive debt from prior borrowing.

sections.title: Nvidia Faces Reputational Damage From Leadership Scandal
points: New York Times reported CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with an Nvidia executive; the Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing to oust him, sending the stock plunging in after-hours trading.

Nvidia stock is down roughly 25% since early October and has been removed from Morgan Stanley's top picks and downgraded to Neutral by Baird, which compared Nvidia to the Icarus myth despite acknowledging the company is 2-3 years ahead on software and silicon.

Investors await results from internal investigations alongside potential inquiries from the FBI and Congress; analysts note an 'espionage-tainted reputation' can linger for years even if legal outcomes favor the company.

sections.title: Consumer Debt Crisis Deepens as Interest Rates Remain Elevated
points: US credit card balances rose $22 billion in Q3 to reach a record $1.28 trillion; credit card interest rates stand near 20%, the highest level since December 2024, forcing Americans to accrue debt faster.
Credit card delinquencies increased in Q3, with the share of people with overdue payments rising 0.3 percentage points to 6.87%, signaling growing strain on household finances.

Holiday spending is expected to exceed $1 trillion this season, according to the National Retail Federation, likely to push credit card debt even higher; higher rates are also affecting mortgages, auto loans, and student debt simultaneously.
